Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 42, verses 1–9:

Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–5} Allah, may He be exalted, informs that He revealed this mighty Qur'an to the Noble Prophet, just as He revealed to those before him among the prophets and messengers. In this is a demonstration of His favor through sending down the books and sending the messengers, both before and after; and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is not an innovation among the messengers; his path is the path of those before him, his circumstances are suited to the circumstances of the messengers before him, and what he brought resembles what they brought, because all of it is truth and sincerity. It is a revelation from One who is characterized by divinity, great might and far-reaching wisdom. Also, the entire upper and lower world belongs to Him and is under His decree and legislative governance; and He is {the Most High} in His essence, His power and His dominion. {The Mighty}: He, by whose greatness {the heavens almost burst apart from above them}: because of their greatness, though they are inanimate; {and the angels}: the noble, close ones, submit to His greatness, humble themselves before His might, and acknowledge His lordship, {exalt their Lord with praise}: glorifying Him above every deficiency and describing Him with every perfection, {and seek forgiveness for those on the earth}: for what proceeds from them that does not befit the greatness and majesty of their Lord; yet He, may He be exalted, is {the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful}: were it not for His forgiveness and mercy, He would hasten to punish creation with a destroying punishment.

In describing Himself, may He be exalted, with these attributes after mentioning that He revealed to all the messengers in general and to Muhammad (ﷺ) in particular, there is an indication that this noble Qur'an contains proofs, evidences and signs that point to the perfection of the Creator, may He be exalted, and to His being described by these great names, which necessitate that hearts be filled with knowledge of Him, love of Him, glorification of Him, reverence for Him, honoring Him and venerating Him, and directing all kinds of outward and inward worship to Him alone. It also indicates that among the greatest injustice and the most abominable speech is taking rivals besides Him, who possess no benefit or harm, but are themselves created beings in need of Allah in all their circumstances.

{6} For this reason He follows it with His saying: {Those who take protectors besides Him}: they befriend them through worship and obedience, just as they worship and obey Allah; they have only taken falsehood, and they are not protectors in reality. {Allah is Watchful over them}: He keeps account of their deeds and will recompense them for their good and their evil, {and you are not a guardian over them}: so that you would be questioned about their deeds; you are only a conveyer of the message, and you have fulfilled your duty.

{7} Then He mentions His favor upon His Messenger and upon mankind in that Allah sent down {an Arabic Qur'an}, clear in its words and meanings, {that you may warn the Mother of Cities}: which is Makkah the Honored, {and those around it}: the settlements of the Arabs; then this warning extends to all of creation. {And warn}: mankind {of the Day of Assembly}: the day on which Allah gathers the first and the last, and inform them that {there is no doubt in it}; and that creation will be divided on that day into two groups: a group {in the Garden}: those who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers, and a group {in the Blaze}: the various kinds of disbelievers who denied.

{8} Despite this, if Allah had willed, He would have made mankind {one community}: upon guidance, for He is the All-Capable who nothing can thwart; but He wills to admit into His mercy whomever He wishes of His chosen creation. As for the wrongdoers who are not fit for goodness, they are deprived of mercy; so they have no protector besides Allah who would take charge of them and attain for them what they love, nor a helper who would repel from them what they dislike.

{9} Those who take protectors besides Him, who befriend them through worshiping them, have erred in the most abominable error; {but Allah is the Protector}: the One whom His servant takes as protector through worship, obedience and drawing near to Him by every possible means of drawing near; and He is the Protector of His servants in general through His governance and the executing of decree among them, and He is the Protector of His believing servants in particular by bringing them out of darkness into light, nurturing them with His kindness, and helping them in all their affairs. {And He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent}; that is: He is the One who disposes of giving life and causing death, and of the execution of will and power; so He is the one who deserves to be worshipped alone, with no partner.

{1–5} Allah, may He be exalted, informs that He revealed this mighty Qur'an to the Noble Prophet, just as He revealed to those before him among the prophets and messengers. In this is a demonstration of His favor through sending down the books and sending the messengers, both before and after; and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is not an innovation among the messengers; his path is the path of those before him, his circumstances are suited to the circumstances of the messengers before him, and what he brought resembles what they brought, because all of it is truth and sincerity. It is a revelation from One who is characterized by divinity, great might and far-reaching wisdom. Also, the entire upper and lower world belongs to Him and is under His decree and legislative governance; and He is {the Most High} in His essence, His power and His dominion. {The Mighty}: He, by whose greatness {the heavens almost burst apart from above them}: because of their greatness, though they are inanimate; {and the angels}: the noble, close ones, submit to His greatness, humble themselves before His might, and acknowledge His lordship, {exalt their Lord with praise}: glorifying Him above every deficiency and describing Him with every perfection, {and seek forgiveness for those on the earth}: for what proceeds from them that does not befit the greatness and majesty of their Lord; yet He, may He be exalted, is {the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful}: were it not for His forgiveness and mercy, He would hasten to punish creation with a destroying punishment.

In describing Himself, may He be exalted, with these attributes after mentioning that He revealed to all the messengers in general and to Muhammad (ﷺ) in particular, there is an indication that this noble Qur'an contains proofs, evidences and signs that point to the perfection of the Creator, may He be exalted, and to His being described by these great names, which necessitate that hearts be filled with knowledge of Him, love of Him, glorification of Him, reverence for Him, honoring Him and venerating Him, and directing all kinds of outward and inward worship to Him alone. It also indicates that among the greatest injustice and the most abominable speech is taking rivals besides Him, who possess no benefit or harm, but are themselves created beings in need of Allah in all their circumstances.

{6} For this reason He follows it with His saying: {Those who take protectors besides Him}: they befriend them through worship and obedience, just as they worship and obey Allah; they have only taken falsehood, and they are not protectors in reality. {Allah is Watchful over them}: He keeps account of their deeds and will recompense them for their good and their evil, {and you are not a guardian over them}: so that you would be questioned about their deeds; you are only a conveyer of the message, and you have fulfilled your duty.

{7} Then He mentions His favor upon His Messenger and upon mankind in that Allah sent down {an Arabic Qur'an}, clear in its words and meanings, {that you may warn the Mother of Cities}: which is Makkah the Honored, {and those around it}: the settlements of the Arabs; then this warning extends to all of creation. {And warn}: mankind {of the Day of Assembly}: the day on which Allah gathers the first and the last, and inform them that {there is no doubt in it}; and that creation will be divided on that day into two groups: a group {in the Garden}: those who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers, and a group {in the Blaze}: the various kinds of disbelievers who denied.

{8} Despite this, if Allah had willed, He would have made mankind {one community}: upon guidance, for He is the All-Capable who nothing can thwart; but He wills to admit into His mercy whomever He wishes of His chosen creation. As for the wrongdoers who are not fit for goodness, they are deprived of mercy; so they have no protector besides Allah who would take charge of them and attain for them what they love, nor a helper who would repel from them what they dislike.

{9} Those who take protectors besides Him, who befriend them through worshiping them, have erred in the most abominable error; {but Allah is the Protector}: the One whom His servant takes as protector through worship, obedience and drawing near to Him by every possible means of drawing near; and He is the Protector of His servants in general through His governance and the executing of decree among them, and He is the Protector of His believing servants in particular by bringing them out of darkness into light, nurturing them with His kindness, and helping them in all their affairs. {And He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent}; that is: He is the One who disposes of giving life and causing death, and of the execution of will and power; so He is the one who deserves to be worshipped alone, with no partner.

{10} God, exalted is He, says: {And whatever you differ about, its judgment rests with God}: concerning the fundamentals of your religion and its branches, whatever you have not agreed upon. {Its judgment rests with God}: it is referred back to His Book and to the Sunnah of His Messenger. Whatever they decide is the truth, and whatever contradicts that is falsehood. {That is God, my Lord}: that is, just as He is the Lord, the Creator, the Provider, the Disposer of affairs, so too He is the One who judges among His servants by His law in all their matters. The implication of this noble verse is that the consensus (ijma') of the Ummah is a decisive proof, because God, exalted is He, has only commanded us to refer to Him what we have differed about. Therefore, what we have agreed upon, the agreement of the Ummah upon it suffices, because it is protected from error, and its agreement must be in accordance with what is in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger. As for His saying {In Him I have put my trust}: that is, I have relied with my heart upon Him in bringing benefits and warding off harms, trusting in God to grant that. {And to Him I turn in repentance}: that is, I direct my heart and body toward Him, toward His obedience and worship. These two foundations God often mentions in His Book, because through their combination the perfection of the servant is achieved, and he loses perfection by losing them or losing one of them; as in His saying: {You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help} and His saying: {So worship Him and put your trust in Him}.

{11} {Originator of the heavens and the earth}: that is, their Creator by His power, will and wisdom. {He made for you mates from yourselves}: so that you may find rest in them, offspring may spread from you, and such benefit as you obtain may come to you. {And of the cattle, mates}: that is, of all their kinds, two types, male and female, so that they may survive and multiply for your many benefits. For this reason He used the preposition lam, which indicates causation: that is, He made that for your sake and for the sake of bestowing blessing upon you. Hence He said: {He multiplies you thereby}: that is, He spreads you and increases you, and increases your livestock, by reason of His having made for you mates from yourselves and mates of cattle for you. {There is nothing like unto Him}: that is, nothing resembles Him, exalted is He, and nothing of His creation equals Him, neither in His essence, nor in His names, nor in His attributes, nor in His actions, because all His names are beautiful, His attributes are attributes of perfection and majesty, and His actions, exalted is He, by which He brought into existence great creatures, were without any partner. So there is nothing like unto Him, by reason of His being unique and singular in perfection from every aspect. {And He is the All-Hearing}: of all voices, in their differing languages, in their varied needs. {The All-Seeing}: He sees the crawling of the black ant, in the dark night, upon the smooth rock, and He sees the flow of nourishment in the organs of very tiny animals, and the flow of water in the fine branches.

This verse and those like it are evidence for the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah) concerning the affirmation of the attributes and the negation of the likeness of creatures. It also contains a refutation of the Mushabbihah (anthropomorphists) in His saying {There is nothing like unto Him}, and of the Mu'attilah (those who deny the attributes) in His saying {And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing}.

{12} His saying: {To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth}: that is, to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the keys of mercy, provision, and apparent and hidden blessings. All creation is in need of God in bringing about their welfare and warding off harms from them in all circumstances; no one has any part of the affair in his hand. God, exalted is He, is the Giver, the Withholder, the Bringer of harm and the Bringer of benefit, and whatever blessing the servants have is from Him alone, and none but He averts evil. What God opens to people of mercy, there is none to withhold it, and what He withholds, there is none to release it after Him. For this reason He said here: {He extends provision to whom He wills}: that is, He widens it and gives of the kinds of provision what He wills. {And restricts}: that is, He straitens it for whom He wills, until it is in proportion to his need, neither exceeding it. All of this follows His knowledge and wisdom. Hence He said: {Indeed He is All-Knowing of everything}: He knows the conditions of His servants, so He gives each what befits His wisdom and what His will requires.

This is the greatest favour that God has bestowed upon His servants: that He has prescribed for them from among the religions the best, the most excellent, the purest and the most virtuous of religions, the religion of Islam. God prescribed it for the chosen and selected among His servants. Indeed, God prescribed it for the best of the best and the elite of the elite, namely the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm) mentioned in this verse, who are the highest of creation in rank and the most perfect in every respect. The religion that God prescribed for them must necessarily be suited to their circumstances and in harmony with their perfection. Rather, God only perfected and chose them because of their adherence to it. Had it not been for the Islamic religion, none of creation would have attained elevation. It is the spirit of happiness and the axis of the wheel of perfection, and it is what this noble Book contains and calls to: monotheism, deeds, morals and manners.

For this reason He said: ﴿That establish the religion﴾; that is, He commanded you to establish all the laws of the religion, its roots and its branches. Establish it yourselves, strive to establish it among others, and cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and transgression. ﴿And do not be divided therein﴾; that is, let there be agreement among you upon the roots of the religion and its branches. Be careful that matters of detail do not divide you and split you into factions, so that you become sects, some of you opposing others, despite your agreement upon the foundation of your religion.

Among the forms of gathering upon the religion and avoiding division within it are the general gatherings commanded by the Lawgiver (al-Shari'), such as the gathering of the pilgrimage (Hajj), the festivals, the Friday congregations, the five daily prayers, jihad, and other acts of worship that are not completed or perfected except through gathering for them and not dividing. ﴿Hard upon the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾; that is, it was extremely difficult for them, in that you called them to sincere devotion to God alone, as He said about them: ﴿And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shudder; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾, and their saying: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ ﴿God chooses for Himself whom He wills﴾; that is, He chooses from His creation whomever He knows to be fit for being selected for His message and His guardianship. Among this is that He selected this community (ummah), preferred it over the rest of the nations, and chose for it the best and most excellent of religions. ﴿And guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾: this is the means by which the servant reaches God's guidance, namely his turning back to his Lord, the attraction of his heart's aspirations toward Him, and his intention of seeking His face. Thus the goodness of the servant's intention, together with his striving in seeking guidance, is among the causes of its facilitation, as the Exalted said: ﴿By it God guides whoever follows His pleasure to the paths of peace﴾.

In this verse, that God ﴿guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, together with His saying: ﴿And follow the way of those who have turned back to Me﴾, and with the knowledge of the conditions of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, and the intensity of their turning back, is evidence that their saying is a proof (hujjah), especially that of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, may God be pleased with them all.

{14} When Allah, the Exalted, commanded the Muslims to unite upon their religion and forbade them from division, He informed them that they should not be deceived by the Book that Allah had sent down to them. For the People of the Book did not split apart until Allah had sent down to them the Book that required unity, and then they did the opposite of what their Book commanded. All of this was out of their transgression and enmity. They hated one another, envied one another, and enmity and rancor arose between them, and so disagreement occurred. So beware, O Muslims, lest you become like them. {And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord}; that is, the postponement of the decisive punishment until a specified term, {the matter would have been decided between them}; but His wisdom and forbearance required that this be delayed for them. {And indeed, those who were given the Book after them}; that is, those who inherited it and became successors to them from among those who claim knowledge, {are in disquieting doubt concerning it}; that is, in great confusion that leads to disagreement, since their predecessors disagreed out of transgression and obstinacy, while their successors disagreed out of doubt and suspicion. All of them share in the blameworthy disagreement.

{15} {So for that, invite}; that is, to the upright religion and the straight path with which Allah sent down His Books and sent His Messengers. Invite your nation to it, urge them upon it, and strive against those who do not accept it. {And be steadfast}: yourself {as you have been commanded}; that is, steadfastness in conformity with the command of Allah, neither neglecting nor exceeding, but complying with the commands of Allah and avoiding His prohibitions, persisting in that. Thus He commanded him to perfect himself by holding to steadfastness, and to perfect others by calling them to that. It is known that the command addressed to the Messenger, peace be upon him, is a command to his nation when no specific restriction to him is stated. {And do not follow their desires}; that is, the desires of those who deviate from the religion, from the disbelievers and hypocrites, either by following them in some part of their religion, or by abandoning the call to Allah, or by abandoning steadfastness. For if you follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would indeed be among the wrongdoers. He did not say "do not follow their religion," because the reality of their religion that Allah legislated for them is the religion of all the Messengers, but they did not follow it; rather, they followed their desires and took their religion as amusement and play. {And say}: to them when they argue and debate: {I have believed in what Allah has sent down of Book}; that is, let your debate with them be founded upon this great principle, which indicates the honor and majesty of Islam and its supremacy over all other religions, and that the religion which the People of the Book claim to adhere to is a part of Islam. In this there is guidance that if the People of the Book debate on the basis of belief in some of the Books or some of the Messengers to the exclusion of others, that is not accepted from them, because the Book to which they call and the Messenger to whom they ascribe themselves must, as a condition, confirm this Qur'an and the one who brought it. Our Book and our Messenger commanded us only to believe in Moses, Jesus, the Torah and the Gospel which he [the Prophet] reported, affirmed, and informed that they confirm him and attest to their authenticity. As for the mere Torah, Gospel, Moses, and Jesus who were not described to us and did not agree with our Book, he did not command us to believe in them.

And His saying: {And I have been commanded to act justly between you}; that is, in judgment regarding what you have disagreed about. Your enmity and hatred, O People of the Book, shall not prevent me from being just between you. Among justice in judging between the people of differing opinions, from among the People of the Book and others, is that what they possess of truth is accepted and what they possess of falsehood is rejected. {Allah is our Lord and your Lord}; that is, He is the Lord of all; you are no more entitled to Him than we are. {For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds}: whether good or bad. {There is no argument between us and you}; that is, once the realities have become clear and truth has become distinguished from falsehood and guidance from error, there remains no place for dispute and contention, because the purpose of debate is only to make clear the truth from falsehood, so that the rightly guided may be guided and the proof may be established against the misguided. It is not meant by this that the People of the Book should not be debated with; how, when Allah says: {And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best}? Rather, what is meant is what we have mentioned. {Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the destination}: on the Day of Resurrection, where He will recompense each according to his deeds, and the truthful will then be distinguished from the liar.

{17} When He (exalted is He) mentioned that His proofs are so clear and evident that everyone who has good in him responds to them, He mentioned their root and foundation. All of it consists of clear signs and manifest evidences for all divine matters and religious beliefs. It came with the finest questions and the clearest proofs.

Whatever goes beyond these two matters, the Book and the Balance, of what is called a proof, an argument, an evidence, or similar expressions, is false and self-contradictory. Its foundations have corrupted, and its structures and branches have collapsed. This is known to whoever has experience with the questions and their sources, and knows how to distinguish the stronger of the evidences from the weaker, and the difference between proofs and fallacies.

As for one who is deceived by ornamented expressions and deceptive words, and whose insight does not penetrate to the intended meaning, he is not of the people of this matter, nor one of the knights of this field. His agreement and his disagreement are equal. Then He (exalted is He) said, warning those who hasten the coming of the Hour and deny it: {And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near}. It is possible that the meaning is: I do not ask you for any reward except one reward, which is for your own benefit and whose benefit returns to you, namely that you love me and be fond of me because of kinship; that is, for the sake of the kinship. On this view, the love is additional to the love of faith. For love of faith in the Messenger, and giving precedence to his love over all other loves after the love of Allah, is an obligation upon every Muslim. Here He asked them for something beyond that, namely to love him for the sake of kinship, because he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had directed his call to those closest to him, to the extent that it has been said that there is no one in the lineages of Quraysh except that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has a kinship tie with him.

It is also possible that the meaning is: except sincere love for Allah, the love that is accompanied by drawing near to Allah and seeking closeness through obedience to Him, which indicates its soundness and sincerity. For this reason He said: ﴿except love in the kinship﴾, that is, in drawing near to Allah.

On both views, this exception is evidence that he does not ask them for any reward at all, except something whose benefit returns to them. This is not, in any way, a reward; rather, it is a reward from him to them, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, and the saying: "Such-and-such has no fault with you except that he is good to you."

﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾: such as prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, or kindness to people. ﴿We will increase for him therein in goodness﴾: by Allah expanding his breast, facilitating his affair, and making it a cause of success for another deed. The believer's deeds increase thereby, and he is elevated with Allah and with His creation, and he attains both immediate and deferred reward. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾: He forgives great sins, however great they may be, when one repents from them, and He rewards small deeds with abundant recompense. By His forgiveness He pardons sins and conceals faults, and by His appreciation He accepts good deeds and multiplies them many times over.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 42, verse 24:

{24} Meaning: Or do the deniers of the Messenger ﷺ say, out of audacity and falsehood: ﴿He has invented a lie against Allah﴾? They have slandered you with the most abominable and ugly of matters, which is fabricating against Allah by claiming prophethood and attributing to Allah what He is free of, while they know your truthfulness and trustworthiness. So how would they dare to tell such a blatant lie? Rather, by this they have also audaciously transgressed against Allah, the Exalted, for it is a disparagement of Allah, since He would have empowered you with this great call which, according to their claim, includes the greatest corruption on earth, by enabling you to declare the call and then attribute it to Him, and then He would support it with manifest miracles, clear proofs, a manifest victory and dominance over those who oppose it. Yet He, the Exalted, is able to cut off this call at its root and source, by sealing up the heart of the Messenger ﷺ so that he would not understand anything and no good would enter it. If his heart were sealed, the whole matter would be ended and cut off. Therefore this is a decisive proof of the soundness of what the Messenger brought, and the strongest testimony from Allah for what he said; there is no testimony greater or more magnificent than it. For this reason, it is part of His wisdom, mercy and established custom that He erases falsehood and removes it, even if it has a surge at certain times, for its end is extinction. ﴿And Allah establishes the truth by His words﴾: by His universal words, which are never altered or changed, and His true promise, and His religious words which realize what He has legislated of the truth, fix it in hearts, and give insight to people of understanding. Indeed, among the completeness of His establishing the truth, He appoints falsehood to oppose it; then when it opposes it, the truth assaults it with its proofs and clear evidences, so that by its light and guidance falsehood is brought to nothing and suppressed, its falsity becomes evident to everyone, and the truth appears in full clarity to everyone. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾: that is, of what they contain, what they are characterized by of good and evil, and what they conceal and do not reveal.

{25} This is an explanation of the perfection of God's generosity, the vastness of His bounty, and the completeness of His kindness in accepting the repentance that comes {from His servants} when they abandon their sins, regret them, and resolve never to return to them, provided they intend thereby the Face of their Lord. God accepts it after their sins had become a cause of ruin and of the occurrence of worldly and religious punishments. So He pardons {the evil deeds} and erases them, erases their traces of defect and what they had required of punishments, and the repentant one returns to Him noble, as though he had never committed any wrong at all; He loves him and grants him success in what brings him closer to Him.

Since repentance is one of the great deeds, it may be complete through the perfection of sincerity and truthfulness in it, it may be deficient when these are lacking, and it may be corrupt if its purpose is to attain some worldly aim. Its locus is the heart, which no one knows except God. Therefore He concluded this verse with His words: {And He knows what you do}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 42, verse 29:

{29} That is: among the proofs of His great power, and that He will bring the dead back to life after their death, is {the creation of these heavens and the earth}, despite their greatness and vastness, which indicates His power and the breadth of His dominion. What is in them of perfection and precise order indicates His wisdom, and what is in them of benefits and interests indicates His mercy. This indicates that He alone deserves all kinds of worship, and that the divinity of anything other than Him is false. {And what He has dispersed in them}; that is, what He has spread throughout the heavens and the earth of the various kinds of living creatures (dawabb), which Allah made as means of benefit and interest for His servants. {And He is, over their gathering}; that is, the gathering of creation after their death for the standing place of the Resurrection, {when He wills, All-Powerful}: His power and His will are sufficient for that, and its occurrence depends on the existence of the true report. It is known that the reports of the messengers and their books have been transmitted in unbroken succession (tawatur) concerning its occurrence.

{30} He, exalted is He, informs that whatever affliction befalls the servants, whether in their bodies, their wealth, their children, or in what they love and what is dear to them, it is only because of what their hands have committed of misdeeds. For God does not wrong the servants, but they wrong themselves. ﴿And if God were to take mankind to task for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back a single creature.﴾

{36} This is a discouragement from the world and an encouragement toward the Hereafter, along with mention of the deeds that lead to it. He says: ﴿So whatever you have been given﴾: of kingship, leadership, wealth, children, health, and bodily well-being, ﴿is but the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾: a pleasure that is tainted and cut off. ﴿And what is with Allah﴾: of abundant reward, great recompense, and lasting bliss ﴿is better﴾ than the pleasures of this world, a superiority with no comparison between them, ﴿and more lasting﴾: because it is a bliss that has no taint, no turbidity, and no transition.

Then he mentions for whom this reward is, saying: ﴿for those who believe and upon their Lord rely﴾. That is, they combined sound faith, which necessitates the outward and inward acts of faith, with tawakkul (reliance on Allah), which is the instrument of every deed. Every deed not accompanied by tawakkul is incomplete. Tawakkul is the reliance of the heart upon Allah to bring about what the servant loves and to ward off what he dislikes, together with trust in Him, exalted is He.

{37} ﴿And those who avoid the major sins (kaba'ir al-ithm) and the immoralities (fawahish)﴾. The distinction between kaba'ir and fawahish, although both are major sins, is that fawahish are the great sins toward which the souls have an inclination, such as fornication and the like, while kaba'ir are those that are not of this kind. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 42, verses 40–43:

{40} God mentions in this verse the levels of retribution, and that they are of three levels: justice (adl), grace (fadl), and wrongdoing (zulm). The level of justice is the requital of an evil deed with an evil deed like it, with no increase and no decrease: a life for a life, every wound for a similar wound, and property is compensated with its like.
The level of grace is pardon and reconciliation with the one who does wrong, and for this He said: ﴿So whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon God﴾; He will recompense him with a great reward and abundant reward. God made reconciliation a condition in pardoning, to indicate that if the offender does not deserve to be pardoned, and the legislative interest (al-maslahah al-shar'iyyah) requires his punishment, then in this case he is not commanded to pardon. Placing the reward of the one who pardons upon God is among the things that stirs one to pardon and to treat creatures in the way one wishes God to treat him. Just as he loves that God pardon him, let him pardon them; and just as he loves that God forgive him, let him forgive them, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.
As for the level of wrongdoing, He mentioned it in His saying: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾: those who transgress against others at the outset, or who retaliate against the offender with more than his offence; the excess is wrongdoing.

{41} ﴿And whoever avenges himself﴾ after ﴿being wronged﴾; that is, whoever avenges himself against the one who wronged him after the wrong has befallen him, ﴿those have no blame upon them﴾; that is, there is no fault upon them in that. His saying ﴿and those who, when tyranny (al-baghy) afflicts them﴾ and His saying ﴿and whoever avenges himself after being wronged﴾ indicate that there must be an affliction of tyranny and wrong and its occurrence. As for the intention to tyrannize others and the intention to wrong them without anything having happened from him, this is not repaid in kind; rather he is disciplined with a discipline that deters him from a word or deed that issued from him.

{42} ﴿Only upon those who wrong the people and transgress in the earth without right﴾ does the blame (as-sabil) lie; that is, the legal punishment is directed as proof only against them. This includes wrong and tyranny against people in their lives, their property, and their honour. ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾; that is, one that pains hearts and bodies in proportion to their wrongdoing and tyranny.

{43} ﴿And whoever is patient﴾ with what he endures of harm from people, ﴿and forgives﴾ them by overlooking what proceeds from them, ﴿indeed that is of the matters of resolve﴾; that is, it is among the matters which God urged and emphasized, and He informed that none attains it except the people of patience and great fortune, and among the matters for which none is granted success except the people of resolve and high aspiration, the possessors of minds and insight. Abandoning retaliation for oneself, by word or deed, is among the hardest things for the self, and patience over harm, pardoning it, forgiving it, and meeting it with goodness is harder and harder still. Yet it is easy for the one whom God makes easy for, who strives against his own self to attain this quality and seeks God's help in that. Then, when the servant tastes its sweetness and finds its effects, he meets it with an open breast, breadth of character, and delight in it.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 42, verses 47–48:

{47} The Exalted commands His servants to respond to Him by carrying out what He has commanded, avoiding what He has forbidden, hastening to do so, and not delaying. {Before there comes}: the Day of Resurrection, which, when it comes, cannot be averted and what has been missed cannot be made up. On that Day the servant has no refuge to which he can flee, escaping from his Lord and running away from Him. Rather, the angels will have encompassed creation from behind them, and it will be called out: {O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond them. You will not pass beyond except with authority}. On that Day the servant has no denial of what he committed and perpetrated; rather, even if he denied it, his limbs would testify against him. This verse and others like it contain a rebuke of false hope and a command to seize the opportunity in every deed that presents itself to the servant, for delay carries calamities.

{48} {But if they turn away}: from what you have brought after the complete clarification, {We have not sent you over them as a guardian}: to guard their deeds and be questioned about them. {Your duty is only to convey}: so when you have discharged what is upon you, your reward has become due from Allah, whether they respond or turn away, and their reckoning is with Allah, who records for them their small and great deeds, their outward and their inward. Then the Exalted mentioned the condition of man: that when Allah causes him to taste mercy, such as bodily health, abundant provision, status, or the like, {he rejoices in it}; that is, he rejoices with a joy confined to it and not exceeding it, and this entails his being content with it and turning away from the Benefactor. {And if an evil befalls them}; that is, sickness, poverty, or the like, {for what their hands have put forward}, {indeed, man is ungrateful}; that is, his nature is ingratitude for the previous blessing and impatience with the evil that has befallen him.

{51} When the disbelievers, who denied the messengers of God, said, ﴿Why does God not speak to us, or a sign not come to us?﴾, out of their arrogance and tyranny, God replied to them with this noble verse, and [showed] that His speaking (ta'alla) occurs only to His special creatures: to the prophets and messengers, and to the elect of the worlds. It occurs in one of these modes: either God speaks to him by inspiration (wahy), casting the inspiration into the heart of the Messenger without sending an angel and without addressing him orally; or He speaks to him orally, but ﴿from behind a veil﴾, as happened to Musa ibn 'Imran, the one God spoke to (Kalim al-Rahman); or God speaks through a royal messenger: He sends ﴿a messenger﴾, such as Jibril or another of the angels, ﴿who reveals by His permission﴾, that is, by the permission of his Lord, not merely by his own desire. Indeed He, exalted, is high in His essence and high in His attributes, great in them, high in His acts, has subdued everything, and all created things are subservient to Him; ﴿All-Wise﴾ in placing everything in its proper place among created beings and legislations.

{52} ﴿And thus﴾, just as We revealed to the messengers before you, ﴿We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾: this is the Noble Qur'an. He called it a spirit because the body is made alive by the spirit, and by the Qur'an hearts and souls are made alive, and by it the interests of this world and the religion are made alive, because of the abundant good and copious knowledge it contains. It is pure favour from God to His Messenger and to His believing servants, without any cause on their part. Therefore He said: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾; that is, before its descent upon you you had no knowledge of the reports of previous scriptures, nor faith and practice of the divine laws; rather, you were unlettered, neither writing nor reading. Then this Book came to you, which ﴿We have made a light, by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾: they illuminate themselves with it in the darknesses of disbelief, innovations and destructive desires, they recognise the realities by it, and they are guided by it to the straight path. ﴿And indeed you guide to a straight path﴾; that is, you make it clear to them, explain it, [and illuminate it], encourage them towards it, forbid them from its opposite, and warn them against it.

{53} Then he explained the straight path, saying: ﴿The path of God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾; that is, the path which God established for His servants, and informed them that it leads to Him and to the abode of His honour. ﴿Unquestionably, to God do all affairs return﴾; that is, all matters of good and evil return to Him, and He will recompense each according to his deeds: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil.
